transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I'm here because... I guess I've just been having these thoughts lately. I keep catching myself thinking that maybe it would just be easier if I went to sleep and didn't wake up. I mean, I haven't made any kind of plan to hurt myself or anything like that, but the thoughts are there, and I figured I should probably talk to someone about it.
Aside from those thoughts, have you been feeling down, sad, or empty most of the day, nearly every day?

Yeah, I have. It's... well, after this burst of energy I had recently wore off, I just felt like somebody had pulled the plug on me. Most days I just sit at the kitchen table, staring at my coffee, feeling completely empty. And... I don't know, just ashamed, really. It's been like that pretty much every day.
During that time when you had that burst of energy, did you feel unusually high, elated, or on top of the world?

Well, I don't know if I'd say I was on top of the world, exactly. It was more like... right after I got fired from my job, I actually felt oddly fired up. Like I had this intense drive to just go out and prove everybody wrong. But at the same time, I was really on edge. I remember snapping at people over just little things, like if someone took too long at the coffee shop. So it wasn't just feeling high, it was a lot of irritability, too.
How long have you been feeling this down and empty?
Well, this low spell... it's been hanging on for about three months now. Pretty much ever since that crash after all that energy I had.
How long did that period of high energy and irritability last?
That high-energy, out-of-control stretch... it lasted about three weeks after I was fired. Then the crash happened.
During those three weeks when your energy was so high, did you find yourself needing much less sleep than usual to feel rested?

Yeah, actually. I mean, there were several nights where I only slept maybe two or three hours tops. But I'd get right up feeling like I had a full tank. I just wasn't tired at all... I felt like I had absolutely no reason to slow down.
During those three weeks, did you feel like your thoughts were racing or moving much faster than usual?

Yeah, they definitely were. My thoughts were just jumping so fast from one thing to another. I'd go from thinking about sales numbers, right to new job leads, then over to beer recipes, or even rehashing old arguments. I really couldn't keep hold of one single idea for more than a few seconds before my mind was already on to the next thing.
During those three weeks, did you do anything unusually impulsive or risky, such as spending large amounts of money or taking chances you normally wouldn't?

No, I didn't really do anything like that. I mean, I had just been fired, so I definitely wasn't going out and spending a bunch of money... didn't have the cash to blow anyway. I didn't take any weird risks or do anything reckless. I was mostly just really wired and stuck in my own head.
During those three weeks when you felt so wired, did you hear or see anything that other people couldn't hear or see?

Yeah, I actually did. It was really strange. When I was all wound up like that, I... I heard my old store manager's voice. It sounded clear as day, like it was coming over an intercom, just telling me to "move the display." But the thing is, I was just sitting all alone in my kitchen when it happened.
